video.title: Working in the Wild (Holly Akello)
video.transcript: Holly Akello doesn’t have an ordinary job! She looks after wild animals at a conservation center in Uganda. Holly is positive and enthusiastic about her job. She likes to be with animals. I feel so lucky that I’m in the field doing what I’ve always dreamed of doing. The 23-year-old takes care of all kinds of animals—from snakes to hyenas. Some people think it’s a dangerous job, but it’s always an adventure, and she loves it! At the conservation center, Holly gets training and learns skills she uses every day. She’s responsible for preparing food and feeding the lions. She gives them their meal. Then she sits down to spend time and communicate with them. I’m not afraid of wildlife. Because, I think, if you’re able to understand them, it becomes so easy for you to work with them. These veterinarians and doctors in Rwanda also think it’s important to look after animals. The team of skilled workers help increase the population of mountain gorillas in the wild. The vets carry equipment with them. They study the gorillas and count them. They give names to the new baby gorillas. See, there is a baby behind, and that baby is on the list to be named. They also teach the schoolchildren in the area about the animals. With the help of the team, the future for these gorillas looks positive! It’s all about teamwork. And of course, each piece makes a difference. You need special skills to work with wild animals every day. And you need to be curious and love adventure—just like these people.

video.title: Marketing and Packaging
video.transcript: Companies know how to make products look exciting to customers. They encourage us to buy certain things. They make them stand out through their designs! Products for men and women often look very different. And the prices are very different. But are the products? Two face products here, same brand. This one is specifically marketed at men; this one is aimed at women. Is there any difference between the ingredients, please? There are a number of ingredients which are the same in each. I can’t see any reason why a chap couldn’t use that. So why do the same products get such different packages? Advertisers carefully choose the packaging and other details to reach a certain audience. Companies like to personalize identical products for different buyers—men and women, for example. The words on the bottles try to get our attention. Advertisers choose the colors this way, too. Grey or blue for men and pink or white for women. And this is not just something that happens with adults. What about children? Why do they want certain products? Studies show they like bright colors. Bright colors make them think of happy times. Kids also like fun characters. So companies put bright colors and fun characters on toys. This makes the toys stand out, and the kids want the item.

audio.title: Annie Griffiths & Explorers
audio.transcript: Ray Bellows: Today we talk with Annie Griffiths. She’s a photographer for National Geographic. Sometimes her work takes her to dangerous places like mountains, under water, or in jungles. Annie: I love southern Africa. I like the energy of the people and the wildlife. I love travel because it allows me to learn about different cultures and different views of the world. I spend time with ordinary people. Ray: How do you communicate if you don’t speak the language? Annie: I get over my shyness. I smile and gesture so people feel relaxed. The most important thing a photographer needs is curiosity. You’ve got to wake up wanting to experience something new. Narrator: What does it take to become an explorer? Explorer can be journalists, scientists, and filmmakers. Bertie Gregory manages film projects. He's responsible for Epic Adventures. If you are enthusiastic about wildlife, work with animals. Step two is to learn photography. Practice taking pictures. You don’t need expensive equipment. Learn other languages. You don’t have to be perfect, but a few words help you make friends. Explorers like new experiences. Sometimes they meet a dangerous animal. Visit places in your own town. There’s a lot of nature in your local park.

audio.title: Nostalgia & Memory Test
audio.transcript: Smell of fresh coffee reminds me of my childhood and my father. Nostalgia brings back good memories. Memory creates an emotion. In the past, people thought nostalgia was about sadness. The word means homesickness. A doctor created the word in 1688 to describe soldiers who missed their homes. Some doctors thought nostalgia was dangerous. Today, it is positive and useful. It helps with change. Thinking about old schools can relax you. It helps when you feel lonely. Doctors play music for older people to help memory. The brain becomes more active. We know much more about memory now. Humans recognize thousands of photos, but we forget others. neuroscientist Wilma Bainbridge created an experiment. Color and appearance are important. We remember 60 percent because of color. We remember photos with people in them.Scientists still do not know why we forget the rest. To make more memories, use the Ten-Year Test. Try 'Firsts' - visit new places. Don't always go the easiest way. Take a different road.
